global_lexicon.core_thesis: Machine learning methods (ANN, SVM, RF, and LSTM) provide superior predictive accuracy and generalization over traditional empirical and mechanistic models for membrane bioreactor (MBR) pollutant removal and membrane fouling, with future implementation hinging on hyperparameter optimization, AutoML, and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI).

key_terms.definition: An advanced wastewater treatment and reclamation technology combining biological treatment (activated sludge) with low-pressure membrane filtration.

The accumulation of foulants (organic compounds, inorganic salts, colloids, and microorganisms) on the membrane surface or within pores, leading to declining permeate flux and increasing transmembrane pressure.
The pressure difference across the membrane that drives filtration, commonly monitored as the principal indicator of fouling progression.

key_terms.term: SVM / SVR (Support Vector Machine / Support Vector Regression)
key_terms.definition: Supervised learning algorithms based on statistical learning theory that use kernel functions to map nonlinear inputs to high-dimensional spaces and maximize margin boundaries.
Information-processing models inspired by biological neural networks, comprising input, hidden, and output layers with interconnected neurons that learn complex nonlinear mappings.
A multilayer feedforward neural network trained via error backpropagation using gradient descent optimization to update synaptic weights.
An ensemble learning algorithm constructed from multiple decision trees using bootstrap aggregating (bagging) and random feature selection to mitigate overfitting.
A recurrent neural network (RNN) architecture equipped with input, forget, and output gates that capture long-term temporal dependencies in dynamic time-series MBR data.
A bio-inspired heuristic search and global optimization algorithm based on natural selection and genetics (crossover, mutation, selection) frequently used for ML hyperparameter tuning.
Systems that automate the end-to-end pipeline of machine learning, including data preprocessing, feature engineering, model selection, and hyperparameter optimization.
Interpretable AI techniques (e.g., SHAP, Garson algorithm, connection weights) that reveal feature contributions and uncover physical mechanisms within black-box models.
An assessment metric measuring the square root of the mean squared differences between observed values and model predictions.
An evaluation metric representing the average absolute difference between predicted and actual observed values.
A statistical measure of goodness-of-fit indicating the proportion of variance in the dependent variable explained by independent features.
High-molecular biopolymers secreted by microbial cells that constitute major foulants forming cake layers on membrane surfaces.

Section Overview:
- Abstract: Summarizes paper scope, MBR fouling challenges, ML advantages over empirical methods, review of ANN/SVM/RF, tutorial example using MATLAB, and future integration with AutoML and XAI.
- 1 Introduction: Water scarcity context, MBR technology advantages, fouling bottlenecks, limitations of empirical/mechanistic models, and rise of ML in MBR research.
- 2 Principles and methods of machine learning:
  - 2.1 Machine learning methods: Taxonomy and architectures of SVM, ANN (MLP, RBFNN, CNN, RNN), Decision Trees/RF, KNN, other methods (ANFIS, ELM, Bayesian), and related algorithms.
  - 2.2 Model optimization: Hyperparameter tuning via grid search, random search, Bayesian optimization, and heuristic algorithms (GA, PSO, SA).
  - 2.3 Assessment of model performance: Evaluation metrics including R², RMSE, MAE, MSE, and cross-validation techniques.
  - 2.4 Assessment of model interpretation: Variable importance and interpretability approaches (Garson algorithm, connection weights, SHAP, LIME).
  - 2.5 Model selection guide: Practical guidelines for selecting ML models based on dataset size, problem type, and operational targets.
- 3 Application of machine learning in MBRs:
  - 3.1 Overview of application: Bibliometric trends, input/output feature distributions, and common modeling workflows in MBRs.
  - 3.2 Machine learning models to predict pollutant removal performances: Application of ML models to predict COD, nitrogen, and phosphorus removal in diverse MBR configurations.
  - 3.3 Machine learning models to predict membrane fouling: Comprehensive review of ANN architectures (3.3.1) and other models (SVM, RF, hybrid models) (3.3.2) for fouling, TMP, and resistance prediction.
- 4 Tutorial example:
  - 4.1 Method: Modeling workflow on virtual MBR dataset using MATLAB, detailing data preprocessing (4.1.1), model selection (SVM, RF, BPNN, LSTM, GA-BP) (4.1.2), and model evaluation protocols (4.1.3).
  - 4.2 Results and discussion: Presentation of raw data profiles (4.2.1) and comparative predictive performance of the five models (4.2.2).
- 5 Summary and prospect: Critical analysis of current challenges (data scarcity, black-box limitations, dynamic operation) and future opportunities (deep learning, AutoML, XAI, digital twins).
- 6 Conclusions: Key summary takeaways of ML application in MBR research and roadmap for intelligent plant operation.
